newsitem.title: UK: Fitch affirms San Diego Gas and Electric.
newsitem.headline: Fitch affirms San Diego Gas and Electric.

text.p: Fitch Investors Service said on Wednesday it affirmed San Diego Gas and Electric Co.'s first mortgage bonds ratings at A plus, and its preferred and preference stock at A.

Fitch said the move followed the announcement to merge San Diego Gas and Electric's parent company, Enova Corp. with Pacific Enterprises, the parent company of Southern California Gas Co., into a new holding company.
"As proposed, the merger will involve a pooling of interests between the parent companies and will leave the utility operating companies' capital structures intact," said Fitch in a statement.
Enova and Pacific expect the merger to be completed before year-end 1997 and before January 1998 -- the opening of the California electricity market to competition, Fitch said.
The agency said its rating reflected the proposed exempt holding company structure, which will keep the utility operating companies segregated.

It said there were also potential synergies to be realized from the merger, including expansion into a new service territory and cost reductions, incremental revenues to be realised from unregulated businesses and the strong credit profile and growth prospects for Pacific.
Fitch said the combination results in projected net cost savings of approximately $1.2 billion over a 10 year period, through combining management and administrative staffs.
Fitch said it is expected, under California law, that roughly 50 percent of cost savings will be passed to customers.

The new company will have a customer base of approximately 6 million - SDG&E serves 1.2 million customers and Southern California Gas serves about 4.7 million customers - the largest number of customers for a U.S. energy utility, Fitch said.

The new company will provide energy and energy related products and services in the unregulated market to consumers first on a regional basis with plans to expand nationally in the future, Fitch said. It also anticipates expanding sales and services to Mexico, the rating agency said.
